chunks: 'Umar ibn Abān narrated to me, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I was in the presence of Abū 'Abdillāh (عليه السلام), and they mentioned the successors, and I mentioned Ismā'īl. So he said: 'No, by Allah, O Abū Muḥammad, that is not up to us, and it is only up to Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He appoints one after another.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام), speaking in this narration
key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلَ: Ismā'īl, mentioned here in discussion regarding succession
key_terms.إِلَى اللَّهِ: belonging to Allah alone; indicating divine determination
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءَ: the designated successors entrusted with divine authority
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; honorific description of Allah
key_terms.وَاحِدًا بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ: one after another; indicating successive divine appointment
key_terms.يُنْزِلُ: He sends down or appoints by divine act

ai.seo_question: Who appoints the Imam according to this hadith from al-Kāfī?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that the designation of the awṣiyā' and the matter of Imamate are not determined by personal choice or family preference. Rather, it is a divine covenant and appointment from Allah, who establishes each Imam one after another.
